PullRequest.Title: Expose all onboarding tours in developer settings
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add persistent onboarding scenario descriptors for developer-setting discovery
- expose archive nudge and transient parallel-work tours alongside all registered session tours
- make the parallel-work developer toggle replay its tour after shared onboarding was shown
- cover descriptor precedence and complete session-tour discovery

## Testing

- rubber-duck review completed and findings addressed
- validation was completed before PR creation; hooks and additional validation were skipped as requested

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed predicate, sole production caller, serial execution path, unconditional on-demand enqueue behavior, and concrete view/overlay work are all directly traced. Only the wall-clock magnitude varies with view state and number of handoffs; the repeated mechanism is deterministic when the toggle remains enabled.
Findings.PerformanceResource: workbench view opening/reveal plus spotlight DOM, target polling, and layout work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With developer mode enabled for the parallel-work tour, the cost repeats once for every qualifying parallel-work handoff in the same window instead of stopping after the first replay; the existing Sequencer serializes these runs but does not suppress later ones.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated main-thread rendering/layout work and repeated sessions-view activation during subsequent parallel-work launches.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous condition always consulted the shared shown key, so after the first new-session or parallel-work tour was shown, later handoffs took the lightweight handoff-only branch and did not open/reveal the Sessions view or construct another spotlight overlay.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new `_hasBeenShown` returns false unconditionally whenever developer mode is enabled for this tour. Every later handoff therefore proceeds through session resolution, `openView`, `revealSessionForOnboarding`, and `runScenario`. `runScenario` is explicitly on-demand and does not apply `_hasBeenShownKey`, so the service's `_shownSinceStart` guard cannot stop these subsequent runs.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 120 adds `return !isOnboardingDeveloperModeEnabled(...) && ...`; when the new developer setting is true, short-circuiting prevents the prior `hasBeenShown(NEW_SESSION_ONBOARDING_SEEN_KEY)` check from ever suppressing later handoffs.
Findings.Title: Keep a session-local guard for developer replay
Findings.Impact: A developer who enables this newly exposed toggle to replay the variation once will pay the full three-step tour rendering path after every additional parallel-work handoff in that window, including reopening/expanding the Sessions view and rebuilding the dimming overlay.
Findings.Evidence: `runWithHandoff` calls `_hasBeenShown` before all expensive tour setup. The added line makes that predicate false for the entire lifetime of developer mode. The reached callback opens `SessionsView` and reveals a row, while `SpotlightPresentation` constructs an overlay, dims the window, resolves/polls targets, and schedules layout for each step. The onboarding service's `runScenario` directly enqueues and presents the scenario without checking shown state, so marking the shared seen key does not restore the fast path.
Findings.Recommendation: Track a separate in-memory "parallel-work developer replay shown" flag (set once this variation is presented/attempted), or otherwise consult a session-local guard before the expensive setup, while still allowing exactly one replay after the shared regular V2 tour was shown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and developer-setting discovery for session onboarding tours
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tour modules register six small descriptors during module evaluation; the onboarding contribution builds and registers the developer-mode configuration schema before/at workbench restoration. This is startup work but remains bounded to the small scenario catalog.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered onboarding scenarios/descriptors; six descriptors are added by this change, with linear map-copy and sort work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous module registration and schema construction; no concurrent fan-out. Later active-scenario registry changes are handled synchronously one event at a time, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Descriptors persist in an in-memory Map for the window lifetime. `getScenarioDescriptors` creates a transient merged Map/array on each schema refresh; there are no cold/warm external cache misses.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that registration adds bounded synchronous allocation/sorting only; module imports and registry/configuration call paths were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future catalog growth is unknown, but current cardinality is tiny and no external boundary or hot-loop execution is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: six small descriptor objects and one bounded startup schema rebuild do not create realistic startup or memory impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal parallel-work handoff after onboarding has already been shown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The incoming `vscode:selectAgentsFolder` IPC dispatch invokes `runWithHandoff`; after the handoff, the shared shown-state check takes the lightweight branch and avoids session resolution, view opening, row reveal, and spotlight rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One incoming IPC event per parallel-work launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC event initiated the same handoff before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC dispatch initiates the handoff; it is pre-existing and not added or multiplied by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Parallel-work handoff events per window; after the first shown tour, effective expensive-work cardinality remains zero for subsequent events when developer mode is disabled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A `Sequencer` serializes handoffs, and replacing `_pending` cancels the prior run; there is no aggregate concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted Memento shown state is the warm-path cache. The changed helper still consults it in normal mode, so warm behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the sole production call site and both branches of `_hasBeenShown` were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for causality; normal-mode performance is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer-mode replay of the parallel-work tour across multiple handoffs in one window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing IPC handoff completes, `runWithHandoff` waits for lifecycle readiness, resolves the session, opens/expands the Sessions view, reveals the row, and synchronously starts the three-step spotlight presentation. The changed developer-mode predicate now sends every later qualifying handoff through this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the existing parallel-work window handoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per launch; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC dispatch occurred, but previously shown state diverted later events to handoff-only processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the scenario path but is not itself introduced or multiplied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and expand the Sessions view, reveal a session row, create/dim a spotlight overlay, poll targets, and schedule layout across three visual steps.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously zero after shared onboarding was shown; now once per qualifying handoff while developer mode remains enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unconditional shared shown-state check prevented all of this setup after the first shown tour.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the underlying handoff but consumes interactive main-thread rendering/layout time and activates the Sessions view for each repeated launch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of qualifying parallel-work handoffs while `onboarding.developerMode['sessions.onboarding.newSessionViewV2.parallelWork']` remains true; one full setup/presentation per handoff, with no once-per-window cutoff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The class-level `Sequencer` serializes runs and replacement cancellation prevents a burst, but completed runs are not coalesced or suppressed, so cost accumulates linearly across handoffs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The service maintains persisted Memento state and `_shownSinceStart`, but the changed helper bypasses the shared shown-state check in developer mode, and on-demand `runScenario` does not apply that cache. Thus warm state does not suppress subsequent work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the changed short-circuit, on-demand service semantics, sole caller, sequencer, and concrete UI work were all inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Developer-mode prevalence and exact rendering duration vary, which limits severity, but repeated reachability and linear event scaling are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated-rendering regression; one finding submitted.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and all diff pages. One introduced repeated-work issue was reported: developer mode disables the only once-per-window guard, causing full view/spotlight work on every later parallel-work handoff. Descriptor catalog changes are bounded startup/in-memory work with no reportable boundary fan-out or retention.
